title: FBI Probes National Crime Database Hack, NASA Mars Rover and Orbiter Hit Glitches, and Startup Sues Apple in India for $162M
subhead: The FBI launched an investigation into an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center database as Signal restricted mobile screenshots over AI surveillance fears, while NASA reported technical glitches aboard a Mars rover and orbiter and a US startup sued Apple in India for $162 million over tap-to-share contacts.

sections.heading: FBI Probes Apparent Hack of Crime Database as Signal Blocks Mobile Screenshots
sections.body:
The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of its National Crime Information Center (NCIC), the central criminal database used by federal, state, and local police across the United States, BBC, NBC News, and TechCrunch report. President Trump called the reported breach 'not good' in remarks to reporters, while the intrusion adds to recent disruptions across US government networks including a classified intelligence outage reported by The Wall Street Journal.

On consumer privacy, encrypted messaging platform Signal restricted screenshot capabilities across both Android and iOS to confront what it called the 'existential threat' of AI surveillance from OS-level agents, criticizing Apple, Google, and Microsoft for lacking developer controls, TechCrunch and The Register report.
sections.whyItMatters: An attack on the FBI's core law enforcement database alongside Signal's anti-screenshot lockdown highlights how both state cyber operations and ambient AI screen capture are eroding data security.

sections.heading: Huang Signals Readiness to Return as Nvidia Stock Drops 48% From Peak
sections.body:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang broke his silence to signal willingness to return to lead the chipmaker amid an SEC accounting investigation and revelations linking associate Alice Huang to funneling restricted GPUs to China, The Wall Street Journal and AFP report. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent nonetheless stated no further export restrictions are needed for Nvidia sales to China, PBS notes.

Across markets, Yahoo Finance and Bloomberg report Nvidia shares have fallen 48% from their peak as a broader AI sell-off wiped out $4 trillion on Wall Street and $1.7 trillion in Chinese AI equities, spilling into crypto. Meanwhile, Nvidia and IBM announced a collaboration using AI to correct quantum computing errors, BigGo Finance reports.
sections.whyItMatters: A 48% drawdown in Nvidia and $5.7 trillion in combined US-China AI market losses show geopolitical export scandals and valuation doubts colliding ahead of Nvidia's post-scandal earnings.

sections.heading: NASA Mars Rover and Orbiter Hit Technical Glitches; SpaceX Starshield Faces Probe
sections.body:
Technical disruptions extended beyond Earth this week as NASA disclosed glitches affecting both a Mars rover and an orbiting spacecraft, complicating ongoing planetary science operations and data relays, The Register reports. Engineers are working to diagnose the twin anomalies without interrupting long-term mission timelines.

In Washington, Breaking Defense and Ars Technica report that US senators are preparing to investigate October 2026 changes to Ukraine's access to SpaceX's Starshield military satellite communications network, warning that abrupt service restrictions raise questions about US defense contractor reliability.
sections.whyItMatters: Simultaneous glitches on aging Mars assets and congressional scrutiny of Starshield highlight operational fragility across both deep-space exploration and commercial military space networks.

sections.heading: Startup Sues Apple in India for $162M Over Tap-to-Share Contacts Feature
sections.body:
A US startup filed a lawsuit against Apple in India seeking $162 million in damages and an injunction that could impact iPhone and Apple Watch imports into the country over Apple's tap-to-share contacts feature, TechCrunch reports.

Elsewhere in consumer and enterprise tech, TechCrunch notes that AI researchers warn nearly everyone in the AI sector is vulnerable to intelligence honey-trap operations, while an actor licensing an AI version of his face to a microdrama startup sparked debate over digital likeness rights in Hollywood. Separately, The Register reports Visa and Mastercard breach researchers found stolen data included phishing clues though not bank-draining credentials.
sections.whyItMatters: Seeking an import injunction against iPhones in India raises the stakes for Apple's fastest-growing manufacturing and consumer market as intellectual property disputes go global.

sections.heading: Nvidia Researchers Question Huge Context Windows as California Eyes Solo AI Antitrust
sections.body:
In AI architecture research, Nvidia scientists argued that massive AI context windows represent a dead end for efficient reasoning and memory scaling, while a separate Nvidia study showed 20,000 targeted training examples sharply boosted AI coding scores, The Decoder and The New Stack report.

On regulation, California's Attorney General signaled readiness to pursue state-level antitrust and AI enforcement independently of federal authorities, Politico reports. Meanwhile, The Register notes AWS is embracing automated bot commerce even as Amazon's main retail site enforces strict bot bans across consumer storefronts.
sections.whyItMatters: Technical skepticism toward brute-force context scaling and aggressive state-level antitrust action in California point to diverging paths for next-generation AI development and oversight.

bottomLine: An apparent hack of the FBI's National Crime Information Center and Signal's mobile screenshot lockdown underscore escalating cyber and AI privacy risks, while Jensen Huang's openness to returning to Nvidia and a $162 million Indian import lawsuit against Apple rattle tech leadership.
sources: BBC, NBC News, TechCrunch, Wall Street Journal, The Register, AFP, PBS, Yahoo Finance, Bloomberg, BigGo Finance, Breaking Defense, Politico
